finding: Six side-by-side-boxplot items that compare TWO groups are labelled 1.8 ("Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics for One Quantitative Variable") instead of 1.9 ("Comparisons of the Distributions for One Quantitative Variable"). This is the same defect shape as the comparison_mislabel class the rework was commissioned to eliminate: a two-group comparison filed under a one-variable topic.
evidence: Each stimulus reads "compared X for two groups ... Construct side-by-side boxplots ... Then compare the typical X and the spread in context". Three of the four rubric criteria per item are comparison criteria: "Uses one interpretable common scale for both groups", "Correctly compares medians in context", "Correctly compares IQR or range in context". E's own SUMMARY.md states the rule it did not apply here: "Both compare-two-groups templates were assigned 1.9". A corpus scan of all items labelled 1.5/1.6/1.7/1.8 found exactly these six carrying two-group comparison language (STATS-MOD3-H006 also matched the scan but is correctly 1.6 -- it describes one bimodal distribution).
recommended_action: Relabel all six to 1.9. This is an adjacent-topic call rather than an absurd one -- boxplot construction is genuinely 1.8 content -- but the dominant construct and three of four criteria are comparison, and E's own stated rule routes compare-two-groups templates to 1.9.

finding: Zero undetermined rows, zero needs_human rows, zero open questions and zero low confidence across all 384 items; 370 high and 14 medium. All six items in E-QA-001 are marked high confidence. The work order explicitly enabled the undetermined sentinel and criticised the prior run for emitting zero of it.
evidence: open_questions.csv is header-only. needs_human='false' on 384/384. The 14 medium-confidence rows are all APSTATS-SFRQ-* with basis 'legacy_metadata_crosswalk' -- confidence tracks metadata provenance, not topical ambiguity, so genuinely ambiguous adjacent-topic calls such as the 1.8/1.9 boxplot family are indistinguishable from certain ones.
recommended_action: Treat 'high' as uninformative for triage on this run. Before the next labelling order, require confidence to reflect topical ambiguity -- specifically, any item where two adjacent topics both fit should be medium or undetermined regardless of metadata quality.

finding: SUMMARY.md states "Both compare-two-groups templates were assigned 1.9" and separately that "graph labels came from subtopics, stimulus, and rubric evidence", but never discloses that six graph items presenting a compare-two-groups task were routed to 1.8 rather than 1.9. A reader of SUMMARY.md alone would conclude the rule was applied uniformly.
evidence: SUMMARY.md sections "Builder judgment calls" and "Named defect classes -- before/after". The generic_graph_stem row reports 20 members and 0 retaining a prior wrong code, which is true, and says nothing about whether the replacement codes are right.
recommended_action: Disclose adjacent-topic routing decisions for a template family in SUMMARY.md, not just the defect-class before/after counts. Zero retained wrong codes is not evidence the new codes are correct.

finding: The prior run was substantially more wrong than its QA established. 140 of the 384 items encode a unit.topic in their content_key (apstat-u<unit>-<topic>-*), an independent author signal E did not claim to use. The prior run agreed with that signal on 9 of 140 (6%); E agrees on 140/140.
evidence: Recomputed from content_key pattern matching against proposed_topic_code. 131 of E's 320 label changes are corroborated by this independent signal. The rejected run's 56 confirmed-wrong items were a sample floor, not a ceiling.
recommended_action: No action. Record so the 83% label churn in this rework is not misread as over-relabelling. It also means any future QA of a labelling run should use the content_key signal as a cheap independent check.
